key_insight: LLMs appear to maintain an implicit, causally manipulable representation of the user, and Belief Self-Distillation (BSD) can both decode and write this user state back into the model.
engineering_relevance: This suggests safety and personalization systems should account not only for the prompt content but also for the model’s inferred beliefs about the user, since these beliefs can materially change outputs like refusals.
method: Frozen LLM self-distills user beliefs from natural conversations.
Learns a compact user representation that is both readable and writable.
Tests causal effects by intervening on the learned belief state and comparing against matched hidden-state steering.
evidence_signal: Across multiple model families, the learned user beliefs were faithfully recovered and interventions on the belief state produced stronger changes than matched steering, including shifts in refusal behavior with the request held fixed.
watch_item: The learned user-state representation may depend on the conversation distribution and could be difficult to validate or control reliably outside the tested model families and settings.
paper_title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
